The point $P(\frac{\sqrt{11}}{6},\frac{5}{6})$ lies on the unit circle, as shown. What is $\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta ?$ Do not round your answer.

$\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta =$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14229367/assets/489a919487ffe7051a27f736ff8ca210e4c246bceac42055e31f5150bc4e094b.png)

Any point $(x,y)$ on the unit circle is related to the central angle $\theta $ as follows:

$$
x=\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta 
$$

We're given that $y=\frac{5}{6}$ at the point $P.$ Therefore, we have

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta =\frac{5}{6}.
$$

Knowing that $\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta =\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta },$ we can calculate $\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta :$

$$
\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta =\frac{1}{(\frac{5}{6})}=\frac{6}{5}
$$
